overview.text: The Indo-Chinese (or Chinese) Rat Snake is a non-venomous rat snake of South-east Asia and southern China, with very large eyes.

identification.text: Head broader than the neck, a blunt projecting snout and very large eyes.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: North-eastern India, Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh through Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, southern China and Taiwan to Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia (Sumatra, Borneo, Java, Bali).

habitat.text: Forests and also near people's homes, up to about 3,000 m.

behaviour.text: Active by day, both on the ground and in trees; it sleeps in bushes and trees.

reproduction.text: Females lay 4 to 12 eggs in June or July.
